content.value_statement: Adding authentication to JavaScript apps can require many framework, database, and security decisions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused Better Auth setup path.
actual_capabilities: Guides new and existing TypeScript or JavaScript projects through Better Auth setup decisions.
Lists required environment variables for secrets, base URLs, and database connections.
Maps server and client auth files to common frameworks and route handlers.
Explains database adapter choices for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Prisma, Drizzle, and MongoDB.
Summarizes migration commands and plugin options for common authentication features.
Provides a security checklist covering cookies, trusted origins, rate limits, email verification, and 2FA.
limitations: It is a concise guide, so users still need the Better Auth documentation for full API details.
It does not verify package versions, framework compatibility, or current provider dashboard settings.
It does not create, store, rotate, or validate production secrets for the user.
Database migration commands should be reviewed before use on shared or production data.

use_cases.title: Start a New Auth Layer
use_cases.description: Plan Better Auth files, environment variables, route handlers, and database setup for a new web app.

use_cases.title: Add Auth to an Existing App
use_cases.description: Identify where Better Auth server, client, and route code should fit into an existing project structure.

use_cases.title: Expand Auth Features
use_cases.description: Choose plugins for 2FA, organizations, admin tools, passkeys, SSO, API tokens, or payments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-auth-skill to plan a basic Better Auth setup for my TypeScript app. Ask me for the framework and database first.

prompt_templates.title: Add Auth to My Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-auth-skill to review my project structure and tell me where Better Auth server config, client helpers, and route handlers should go.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Database Migrations
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-auth-skill to compare Better Auth migration steps for my selected adapter. Include what I should review before running commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design Enterprise Auth
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-auth-skill to design a Better Auth plan with SSO, organizations, admin management, session checks, and production security controls.

output_examples.input: Plan Better Auth for a new Next.js app using PostgreSQL.
output: A short implementation plan covering the auth config location, client helper file, route handler, database adapter, and migration review step.
A checklist of required environment variables and production security settings.

output_examples.input: Add passkeys and 2FA to an existing Better Auth setup.
output: A plugin plan that separates server plugin needs, client plugin needs, migration impact, and user interface updates.
A reminder to re-run migrations after plugin changes and test recovery flows.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot invalid origin errors after deployment.
output: A focused diagnostic path for base URL settings, trusted origins, cookie behavior, and provider redirect settings.

best_practices: Confirm the framework, database adapter, and deployment target before generating auth files.
Review generated migrations and plugin schema changes before applying them to important data.
Use the security checklist before release, especially secure cookies, trusted origins, rate limits, and 2FA needs.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real database URLs, OAuth secrets, or Better Auth secrets into prompts.
Do not run migration commands on production data without review, backups, and rollback planning.
Do not enable account linking, SSO, or admin plugins without checking their access rules.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and implement Better Auth in TypeScript and JavaScript applications.

faq.question: Can it work with existing applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a path for adding Better Auth to an existing project without current authentication.

faq.question: Which frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The guide references Next.js, Express, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Hono, React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and vanilla JavaScript clients.

faq.question: Does it handle database migrations?
faq.answer: It lists migration approaches for built-in Kysely, Prisma, and Drizzle, but users must review commands before running them.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets?
faq.answer: No. It names required environment variables, but users must generate and store secrets securely.

faq.question: Is it only for simple login forms?
faq.answer: No. It also covers plugins for 2FA, organizations, admin tools, API tokens, passkeys, SSO, SCIM, and payments.
